newDescription:
In this Year 3 Maths lesson, pupils learn to compare and order unit and non-unit fractions. They use bar models to see how the numerator and denominator affect the size of a fraction and practise arranging fractions in ascending and descending order.

This lesson includes:
✔ Revising unit fractions, which have a numerator of one, and non-unit fractions
✔ Comparing unit fractions using equal-sized bar models
✔ Understanding why a smaller denominator makes a unit fraction greater
✔ Ordering unit fractions in ascending and descending order
✔ Comparing fractions with the same denominator by comparing their numerators
✔ Comparing fractions with the same numerator by comparing their denominators
✔ Explaining why, for fractions with the same numerator, the smaller denominator gives the greater fraction
✔ Ordering fractions with the same denominator from smallest to greatest and greatest to smallest
✔ Ordering fractions with the same numerator in ascending and descending order
✔ Using bar models and the relationships between numerators and denominators to justify comparisons
✔ Completing independent practice and checking answers on pre-lesson sheets

Pupils begin by sorting unit and non-unit fractions, then compare unit fractions using bar models of equal-sized wholes. They learn that when the numerator is one, a smaller denominator represents a larger fraction, and apply this rule to order unit fractions.

The lesson then develops comparison of fractions with the same denominator. Pupils see that the parts are the same size, so the fraction with the greater numerator is greater. They also compare fractions with the same numerator, learning that the smaller denominator gives the greater fraction because each part is larger.

Pupils use bar models to explain their reasoning and practise ordering fractions with the same denominator and the same numerator in both ascending and descending order. Worked examples and independent practice help them apply the correct rule in each situation.

By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to compare and order unit and non-unit fractions, explain how numerators and denominators affect fraction size, and use bar models and the appropriate comparison rules to arrange fractions accurately.
